records.description: "When the user reports 'X is broken / X is down / fix it' WITHOUT context (just an error message, symptom, or 'down' claim), the agent's job is NOT to take destructive action. Run independent multi-path live probes FIRST across the claimed-broken surface (state, network, services, recent changes), report evidence with strict Return Shape (terse table per substrate), and ask for clarification before any destructive action. The user often has partial info — the actual cause is usually a different layer (wrong URL, missing DNS, stale config) than the user assumes. Codified from 2026-07-19 session where 'proxmox is down' turned out to be a wrong-URL perception and 'OpenID redirect failed' turned out to be a Tailscale mesh exposure issue, both with full Proxmox+DNS health confirmed live. records.name: Wsl-process-cleanup
records.plain: Clean up resource-hungry or unwanted processes on WSL2 when system systemd is disabled.
records.description: Clean up resource-hungry or unwanted processes on WSL2 when system systemd is disabled. WSL2 has TWO systemd layers — system systemd AND user systemd — and many services (Paseo, langgraph, ttyd, mcp_stdio_watchdog-spawned children) live in user systemd with Restart=always, making naive `pkill` futile. Use when the user reports "memory is tight on WSL", "I keep killing X but it comes back", "what's eating all my RAM", "Paseo keeps respawning", "docker keeps coming back", "gws-mcp keeps respawning", or wants a service audit that distinguishes (1) plain processes you can kill, (2) Restart=always services that need `systemctl --user disable`, (3) MCP children managed by mcp_stdio_watchdog that respawn instantly. Class-level — applies to any WSL2 instance where system systemd is disabled but user systemd is alive.
